messages:
kai: Quick heads-up — saw ~12% 99p latency regression on host ingress after kernel-picker roll. Repro on bench with replayed traffic.

devon: https://perf.redwood/internal/ingress/17623 — looks like increased user CPU in parse stage, not GPU.

marie: Did we roll kernel-picker changes yesterday? I only remember the generic-fallback tweak.

alan: Yep, rolled kernel-picker v2 that prefers avx-generic for short sequences. Fallbacks might hit different codegen paths.

kai: Quick profiling snapshot (trimmed):
```
parse_stage 45% cpu
kv_cache 12%
syscall 8% (writev)
grpc 20% (small writes + HPACK)
userland_tokenize 15%
```

sre-jen: @kai can you paste the pprof or a flame? My hunch is syscall flushes (many small writev) are killing tail.

kai: pprof snippet (trim):
```
# top
parse::tokenize 35%
parse::frame_assembler 25%
grpc::writev_dispatch 10%
kv::evict_scan 8%
```

devon: frame_assembler spike + writev points at smaller streaming chunk sizes after the preparse changes -> more syscalls.

marie: Also saw batching heuristics changed: min_batch=2 for latency. That reduces batching on short chats and increases syscall count. :thinking_face: 

alan: Another angle: kernel-picker v2 picks K_g for seq<32. K_g's memory access pattern does per-token KV lookups (non-vectorized) which can thrash hot KV shards.

kai: Repro command I used: `./bench --replay fixtures/10k_short_chats --kernel-picker=v2 --min-batch=2 --http2=on`

bench-bot: Quick bench diff (baseline -> v2):
- p50: 8ms -> 9ms
- p95: 22ms -> 26ms
- p99: 48ms -> 54ms

sre-jen: Can we try toggles to isolate cause? kernel-picker=v1 vs v2, and bump min_batch to 4. Also try host-proxy write coalescing.

devon: Did quick toggles locally:
- kernel-picker=v1 + min_batch=4 -> p99 back to 46ms
- kernel-picker=v2 + min_batch=4 -> p99 50ms
- kernel-picker=v2 + min_batch=2 + host-coalesce=true -> p99 49ms

marie: So both kernel selection and batching heuristics matter. KV evict shows up in pprof too — maybe K_g's layout increases cache misses causing more evictions.

alan: Proposed short plan:
1) Reproduce at scale on perf harness and collect full pprof traces.
2) Add lightweight instrumentation: token_count per request, writev_count, kv_cache miss/evict counters.
3) Make kernel-picker soft: prefer K_g only if batch >= N or seq<Y AND batch>1.
4) Add small writev coalescer at host-proxy (window ~200us) as opt-in.
5) If rollback needed, revert kernel-picker roll for canary.

kai: I'll spin a canary with kernel-picker soft-fallback + no write coalesce. cc @marie @devon

marie: Also add a microbenchmark targeting KV shard eviction pattern under K_g layout so we can confirm hypothesis.

infra-bot: Deployment started: canary -> 3 hosts, kernel-picker.soft_fallback=true, host_coalesce=false

kai: Canary telemetry after 1h: p99 down from 54ms -> 50ms. writev rate -18%. kv_evict rate ~unchanged.

devon: Nice. If we turn on proxy coalescing we might shave another 2-4ms.

alan: Caveat — HPACK & http2: if coalesce window is too long we might increase latency due to HPACK state and head-of-line interactions. Keep window <= 250us. :warning:

sre-jen: I'll add an alert rule: if writev_per_sec spikes AND p99 > 50ms -> page on-call.

kai: Thanks all — I'll attach full traces and open an issue with checklists. Will also include the bench commands and pprof artifacts.

marie: Great, thanks. tagging follow-ups in the issue. :+1:
